title: Safe orchestration for heterogeneous rollouts with pin coherence
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: When performing A/B or canary rollouts across heterogeneous regions and capacity tiers we must guarantee pin coherence: sessions or tokens that have been pinned to a model variant should not be silently routed to incompatible fallback variants, or to a different region/tier that breaks latency/consistency expectations. Current routing heuristics allow escape paths during capacity exhaustion and cross-region failover that can violate business invariants (e.g., session continuity, feature flag semantics).
decision_log: 2026-02-23: Decided to enforce a two-layer guard: a deterministic pin resolver + lightweight policy envelope evaluated at routing time to guarantee compatibility between pinned variant and chosen fallback.

2026-02-26: Chosen approach stores minimal pin metadata (variant id, pin_ttl, origin_region, origin_tier) in session context and in the orchestrator's sticky-affinity index rather than full session objects to limit storage growth.

2026-03-03: Agreed to treat model-compatibility as a first-class property in the model catalog; each model variant must publish a compatibility vector (api schema, tokenizer id, max-seq, quantization family) for safe downgrade routing.

2026-03-07: Opted not to embed a full probabilistic decay into core routing for now; instead implement deterministic TTL + optional graduation hook for explicit session graduation on successful responses.
tasks: Design API change: extend routing decision context with pin_meta (variant, pin_ttl, origin_region, origin_tier). -- Sofia
Model catalog: add compatibility_vector schema and backward-compatibility tags. -- Research/Applied ML
Runtime: implement deterministic pin-resolver that returns a ranked set of valid fallback variants with compatibility scoring. -- Liam
Orchestrator: add policy envelope evaluation and add instrumentation points for fallback reasons. -- Orchestration team
E2E tests: build staged scenarios (region outage, tier degradation, capacity spike) in staging harness. -- SRE
Docs/Console: add rollouts UI hints and warnings when a pinned cohort will be affected by chosen fallback. -- Developer Experience
acceptance_criteria: Pinned sessions maintain variant compatibility: sessions pinned to variant V1 must never be routed to variant Vx if compatibility_vector(Vx) is incompatible with V1's required features.
Fallback ranking respects origin_region and origin_tier preferences unless explicit cross-region failover policy is enabled for the customer.
Pin TTL honoured: TTL renewal only occurs via explicit graduation API or when the original variant serves a successful response and the routing policy permits extension.
Observability: fallbacks and pin-violations are surfaced in the Console (per-route breakdown) with counts and example request IDs.
Performance: route resolution latency overhead < 1ms p50 on production-like load in staging cluster.
implementation_notes: Use existing sticky-affinity index but change value schema to small token: "v:<variant>|t:<expiry>|r:<region>|z:<tier>" to keep Redis memory minimal.

Add compatibility_vector fields to model metadata: {schema_version, tokenizer_hash, input_shape, supported_quant_families}. Keep as flat tags in catalog to match JSON schema requirements in the console.

Routing algorithm: 1) resolve pin_meta from request/session key; 2) query model catalog for candidate variants in preferred region/tier; 3) filter by compatibility_vector superset relation; 4) if empty, consult fallback policy: either allow degraded compatibility (with alerting) or route to dedicated compatibility variant; 5) record reason code for observability.
Persistence: ensure TTL collision safety when two clients attempt concurrent pin renewals; use check-and-set semantics on the sticky-affinity store.
Backward compatibility: default behavior for customers not opting into new pin_meta is unchanged; rollout behind a feature flag.
test_plan: Unit tests for compatibility_vector matching and superset logic.

Integration test: simulate pinned session hitting region with no compatible variants -> verify orchestrator follows 'degrade=false' policy and triggers explicit fallback route to compatibility variant.
Load test: route resolution microbench under synthetic QPS matching 2x peak regional traffic; ensure <1ms added latency.
Chaos scenarios: drain a capacity pool while pinned cohorts are present; validate automatic canary split honors pin TTL and does not reassign pinned sessions mid-request.
Observability tests: ensure fallback events generate a dashboard row and that example request IDs are queryable in the Console tracing view.
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated in staging on 2026-03-12 for internal teams.
Alpha rollout to 2 internal customers with low-latency SLAs on 2026-03-18 for 48h monitoring window.
Gradual ramp to 20% of production traffic in region-us-west over 72h if no alerts; monitoring window includes error rate, tail latency, and fallback ratio.
If fallback_ratio > 0.5% or user-visible error rate increases > 0.1ppt, auto-roll back via feature flag and trigger incident review.
Full rollout to all customers by runtime-2.6 GA after 2 successful canaries and sign-off from SRE and Product.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Missing or incorrect compatibility metadata for older model variants could cause unnecessary fallbacks. Mitigation: default to conservative compatibility (no downgrade) and provide a migration script to backfill catalog tags.
Risk: Sticky-affinity store growth. Mitigation: compact pin_meta token and TTL-based eviction; provide background TTL purge job.
Risk: Increased routing latency. Mitigation: benchmark algorithm, cache last-resolved fallback lists per-session for short window (e.g., 10s) and measure p99.
Risk: Customer confusion when sessions appear to be "stuck" on an older variant. Mitigation: Console shows cohort pin status and provides a manual 'graduate session' action for support.
